paragraphs.source_en: “No matter how many more times you hit him, it will be just the same, won’t it?” So saying, my master’s wife struck me once more on the head with the palm of her hand. It still did not hurt in the least, and I remained silent. But why they were hitting me like this was, for all my deep cunning, quite beyond my comprehension. If I could have understood it, I might have found some suitable countermeasure; but since my master merely kept telling his wife to hit me, not only was the wife who did the hitting at a loss, but I, the one being hit, was at a loss as well. Having twice failed to get what he wanted, my master said, with a touch of impatience, “Here, hit him so that he meows!”

paragraphs.source_en: With a look of annoyance, my master’s wife said, “What do you want to make him meow for?” And with that she bestowed another slap upon me. Now that I knew the other party’s purpose, the matter was simple. All I had to do was utter one cry, and I could satisfy my master. It is because my master is such a fool that I find him so disagreeable. If the object was to make me meow, he should have said so from the start; then there would have been no need to hit me two or three extra times, and I would not have had to undergo the beating two or three times over when once would have freed me. If hitting was not the purpose, then he ought not to have issued the command to hit. Hitting and meowing are not acts performed by the same person. To assume from the beginning that I would meow if struck, and to suppose that the command to hit somehow included the meowing, which ought to be at my own discretion, is an overbearing attitude, an act of disrespect for another’s personality, and a way of looking down on cats. It would be just the sort of thing Kaneda, whom my master hates as one hates a snake or scorpion, might do; but for my master, who prides himself on naked honesty, it is decidedly base. To tell the truth, however, my master is not so mean a man as that, and therefore this command of his did not spring from the height of cunning. I judge it to have arisen simply from a deficiency in my master’s intelligence. Perhaps it was merely the result of his simple-minded reasoning: if one eats, the belly swells; if one is cut, blood comes out; if one is killed, one dies. And so he concluded in haste that if he hit me, I was bound to meow. But I am sorry to say that this is rather lacking in logic. If one reasons on that pattern, then falling into a river must always mean drowning, eating tempura prawns must always mean diarrhea, receiving a monthly salary must always mean going to work, and reading books must always make one a great man. If all these things were necessarily so, certain people would find themselves in some difficulty. And if it is held that I must always meow when struck, that too is a nuisance to me. If I am to be regarded like the bell at Gokokuji, ringing whenever it is struck, then what was the point of being born a cat? Having first thus taken my master down a peg or two in my heart, I then went “meow!” and cried as ordered.

paragraphs.source_en: His wife gave no answer to this exceedingly sudden question. To tell the truth, even I thought that this bizarre question had burst forth because the hot bath had made him lightheaded. Originally, my master was famous throughout the neighborhood as an eccentric, and some people even declared outright that he suffered from nervous disease. Yet my master’s self-confidence is extraordinary, and he stubbornly insists, “I am not the one with nervous disease; it is the people of the world who are diseased.” When the neighbors call my master a yapping “mad dog,” he, in order to preserve fairness, calls them “stupid pigs.” It seems my master truly intends to preserve fairness to the very end; there is no helping him. Since he is this sort of man, putting such a strange question to his wife may be, for him, no more than a trifling incident before breakfast. But from the hearer’s point of view, it is exactly the sort of thing one would expect from someone rather close to nervous derangement. Thus my master’s wife was quite bewildered and said nothing at all. As for me, of course, I had no idea how to answer.
